scope: Developer-only stdio blueprint reference wrapper around unchanged production server factory; no snapshot, game/provider call, construction or player integration.
checks: Actual stdio initialize/list_tools exposes exactly two additional read-only tools; every original tool definition equals a separately instantiated production server definition.
Summary search omits geometry and reports requested/reviewed versions and catalog checksum. Explicit get returns the original grid with source/author/rights/catalog evidence and caveats.
Other version stays unknown, no match is empty, unknown ID and nested execution/Boolean-limit/path arguments return expected tool errors.
Actual returned content is one JSON text block within 64-KiB UTF-8 bounds. Independent Unicode near-bound/overflow and NaN checks verify serialization refusal.
CLI requires an existing explicit disposable subdirectory strictly under repository runtime and refuses missing/default/outside/root/symlink paths.
No snapshot is supplied for reference retrieval; no live-state/UI/session evidence is invented. Registry/client results preserve no-construction/no-execution qualifiers.
limits: Developer entry point only. The published production server/coordinator/player tool admission remains nineteen, and provider access to these two tools is not integrated or tested.
Nested tool request schemas are strict; this is not a general MCP transport/adversarial-server or every possible malformed-envelope audit.
State-directory checks are explicit developer isolation, not a race-resistant OS security boundary against another process changing the filesystem.

Original teaching geometry/catalog evidence retains its earlier native scope/date. No new native, paid inference, community/video geometry/rights, construction, physical UI or paired player release acceptance is claimed.
